item.title: CARMEN.maquia Ballet Hispánico — Feb 4, 2027
item.description: Lied Center Main Stage Thursday, February 4, 2027 · 7:30 PM Bizet's Carmen has seen countless interpretations over the past 150 years, but never one like this. Acclaimed choreographer Gustavo Ramírez Sansano brings this full-length ballet to the stage, inspired by tauromaquia – the art of bullfighting – breathing a modern life into this legendary character. Highly original and full of explosive movement that leaves you breathless, CARMEN.maquia is a bold reimagining of this tragic tale presented by Ballet Hispánico New York, the... Source: Lied Center for Performing Arts

item.title: Orpheus Chamber Orchestra — Feb 17, 2027
item.description: Lied Center Main Stage Wednesday, February 17, 2027 · 7:30 PM GRAMMY® award-winning Orpheus Chamber Orchestra returns to the Lied with British virtuoso pianist Isata Kanneh-Mason for an evening of elegance and vitality. The program pairs classical favorites by Mozart and Haydn with selections from Handel’s Water Music Suite and a newly commissioned work by Katie Jenkins, showcasing Orpheus’ trademark conductor-less precision and collaborative spirit. Source: Lied Center for Performing Arts

item.title: Piano Battle — Mar 20, 2027
item.description: Lied Center Main Stage Saturday, March 20, 2027 · 7:30 PM It’s classical music like you’ve never seen it before! In Piano Battle, virtuoso pianists Andreas Kern and Paul Cibis go head-to-head in a thrilling, interactive competition where the audience decides the winner of each round. Blending dazzling technique with humor and showmanship, this high-energy performance transforms a traditional recital into an unforgettable musical showdown. Who performs it best? You decide! Source: Lied Center for Performing Arts

item.title: Daniil Trifonov — Mar 22, 2027
item.description: Lied Center Main Stage Monday, March 22, 2027 · 7:30 PM Praised as “the most astounding pianist of our age” by London’s The Times, GRAMMY® Award-winning pianist Daniil Trifonov makes his Lied Center debut with a program showcasing extraordinary range. Handel’s Suite No. 5 in E Major (“The Harmonious Blacksmith”) opens the concert followed by Stravinsky’s sole piano sonata and Schubert’s beloved “Wanderer Fantasy,” a powerful musical depiction of a stranger’s search for meaning and happiness in a... Source: Lied Center for Performing Arts
